title: Keeping a Remote Audience Awake
meta: B2 · 约 290 词 · 场景：线上汇报

sections.heading: 1. You Are Competing with Their Inbox
paragraphs: In a meeting room, you can see when people ==drift== away.
On a video call, you see a grid of muted squares, half of them with cameras off.
Somewhere behind those squares, your audience has email, chat, and a dashboard they are quietly ==monitoring==.
This means a remote talk cannot be the same talk you would give in person.
Your slides are not just competing with silence; they are competing with every notification on the listener's screen.
**Online, attention is not something you earn once; you have to win it back every few minutes.**
The good news is that small changes make a big difference.
You do not need to be more ==charismatic==, you need to be more ==deliberate== about rhythm.
sections.heading_zh: 1. 你在跟他们的收件箱抢注意力
paragraphs_zh: 在会议室里，你能看出大家什么时候走神了。
在视频会上，你看到的是一格格静音的小方块，一半还关着摄像头。
在那些小方块后面，你的听众开着邮件、聊天工具，还有一个他们正在悄悄盯着的看板。
这意味着远程分享不能照搬线下的讲法。
你的幻灯片不只是在跟沉默竞争，它在跟听众屏幕上的每一条通知竞争。
在线上，注意力不是赢一次就完事的，你得每隔几分钟就重新把它抢回来。
好消息是，小小的改变就能带来很大的不同。
你不需要更有个人魅力，你需要更刻意地把控节奏。

sections.heading: 2. Change Something Every Five Minutes
paragraphs: Plan your talk in short blocks, and make sure something changes at the end of each one.
Switch from slides to a live screen, ask a question, or ==hand over== to a colleague.
**A change in what people see or hear pulls their eyes back to your window.**
Use the chat ==actively==, because it is easier than unmuting.
"Type one if you've hit this bug, and two if you haven't."
Within seconds, the room __comes alive__, and you have real data to react to.
Call on people by name, but warn them first.
"In a minute, I'll ask Hana how her team handles alerts."
Hana starts listening ==closely==, and so does everyone else, because they know it could be them next.
Finally, __cut your content__ by about a third compared with an in-person version.
Remote listeners tire faster, and nobody has ever complained that a call ended early.
Leave the details in a written doc, and __use the live time__ for the parts that need a conversation.
paragraphs_zh: 把分享拆成一个个短小的模块，确保每个模块结束时都有点变化。
从幻灯片切到实时屏幕、抛一个问题，或者交给同事来讲。
大家看到的或听到的一有变化，视线就会被拉回你的窗口。
多用聊天框，因为打字比解除静音容易。
「遇到过这个 bug 的打一，没遇到过的打二。」
几秒钟之内，全场就活跃起来了，你也有了可以回应的真实数据。
可以点名，但要先打个招呼。
「等会儿我会问问 Hana，她们团队是怎么处理告警的。」
Hana 会开始认真听，其他人也一样，因为他们知道下一个可能就是自己。
最后，内容要比线下版本砍掉三分之一左右。
远程听众更容易累，而且从来没人抱怨过会议提前结束。
细节留在书面文档里，现场时间用在需要讨论的部分。

gist.q: 作者认为线上汇报和线下汇报最大的不同是什么？
gist.a: 线上看不到听众的状态，而且你在和他们屏幕上的邮件、消息、通知争夺注意力，注意力需要每隔几分钟重新赢回。

gist.q: 作者建议多久做一次变化？可以怎么变？
gist.a: 大约每五分钟；切换到实时画面、提一个问题、交给同事讲，或让大家在聊天框里回复。

gist.q: 点名提问时作者有什么技巧？内容量应怎样调整？
gist.a: 提前预告要点谁，让对方和其他人都专心听；内容比线下版本削减约三分之一，细节放到书面文档。

prompts.q: 你在给几个海外团队做线上分享，讲到第十分钟，感觉大家都在干别的。用 30 秒做一次“变化”：用聊天框互动，并预告接下来要点名。
prompts.ref: Let me pause the slides for a second and get a quick pulse check. In the chat, type one if your team has had a deploy rolled back this quarter, and two if not. Okay, I'm seeing lots of ones, that's what I expected. In a moment, I'm going to ask Carlos what his team changed after their last rollback, so Carlos, get ready.
prompts.ref_zh: 我先暂停一下幻灯片，快速摸个底。在聊天框里，如果你们团队这个季度有过部署被回滚，就打一，没有就打二。好，我看到好多一，跟我预想的一样。等会儿我会请 Carlos 讲讲他们团队上次回滚之后改了什么，Carlos 准备一下。

prompts.q: 你要把一个六十分钟的线下培训改成线上版本。用 30 秒向同事说明你打算怎么调整结构。
prompts.ref: For the online version, I want to cut it down to about forty minutes. I'll split it into short blocks of five or six minutes each, and end every block with something different, a poll in the chat, a quick live demo, or a question for a specific person. The detailed examples will go into a written guide that people can read afterward, so the live time is mostly discussion.
prompts.ref_zh: 线上版本我想压缩到四十分钟左右。我会把它拆成每段五六分钟的短模块，每段结尾都换个花样，比如聊天框里的投票、一段简短的现场演示，或者点名问某个人一个问题。详细的例子会放进一份书面指南，大家会后可以看，这样现场时间主要用来讨论。

words.ex: I could see people drift away during the long architecture section.
Keep monitoring the error rate for an hour after the deploy.
You don't have to be charismatic to give a clear tech talk.
Keeping the first release small was a deliberate choice.
We're actively looking into the login failures.
We'll watch the memory usage closely during the canary.
The retro really came alive once we started using sticky notes.
Feel free to call on me if you need the backend view.
I mute all notifications when I'm on call for deep debugging.
I'll hand over to Mei for the database part of the demo.
